criteria.expectedOutcome: Collaborative departmental agents negotiate schedules under operational windows, qualified rosters and owner-approved fatigue rules, identify collisions, propose alternate allocations and ensure every applicable SFTRM periodicity is satisfied.
criteria.reason: The slice demonstrates deterministic feasibility for synthetic departmental requests only. No collaborating agents, authoritative fatigue policy, SFTRM rules or completion history are supplied. Full source requirement remains unverified.

criteria.expectedOutcome: Every complete proposal has zero overlapping interval pairs sharing personnel or an exclusive resource. In the planned two-request example, Damage Control occupies Monday 09:00–10:00 UTC and Engineering moves from 09:00 to 10:30–11:30 UTC; both use Alex and Room A without overlap. Proposal edits invalidate prior review.

Within explicit synthetic inputs, every assigned interval is contained in a ship operating window and every assigned person availability window, all required qualifications are covered by assigned people, every same-person pair satisfies supplied rest and total horizon duty does not exceed budget. Missing FPL, availability ending at minute 600, rest 31 and duty budget 119 prevent the two-request proposal; restoring availability to 1020, rest 30 and budget 120 yields both requests and exactly 120 duty minutes. These are demonstration values, not approved policy.

An exhaustive search of the impossible two-request candidate set reports Infeasible: no complete schedule within supplied candidates. A one-node budget reports Search limit reached: feasibility is unknown. Neither exposes an approvable partial proposal. Invalid duration is rejected as validation, separate from either solver result. Correcting inputs or increasing budget recovers a complete feasible proposal.

Expand every applicable owner-supplied mandatory recurrence rule into uniquely identified occurrences and due windows, accounting for completion history and horizon boundaries; every mandated occurrence is scheduled by its deadline with no omissions.
criteria.reason: Owner-approved periodicity rules, applicability and completion history are missing. Two explicit synthetic occurrences do not establish recurrence completeness or SFTRM compliance. No mandatory-compliance indicator will be shown.

criteria.expectedOutcome: An authorized PB4T operator reviews the editable proposal, personnel loading and every requested constraint change and explicitly accepts that exact validated schedule; any changed input requires renewed review.
criteria.reason: Local revision-bound acceptance and edit protection are demonstrated, but automated interaction cannot establish actual operator acceptance. No authorized operator or human acceptance evidence is supplied. Hard constraints are never relaxed automatically.

criteria.expectedOutcome: An interactive weekly board automatically resolves cross-department conflicts, provides one-click schedule optimization under an agreed objective, and displays correct personnel loading heatmaps.
criteria.reason: The prototype supplies a weekly editable board, conflict comparison, one-action feasible allocation and numeric heatmap. Bounded first-feasible search has no optimization objective or optimality guarantee; the full deliverable remains unverified pending owner definition and implementation of optimization.
